title: TypeScript Starter
description: Add type annotations to small functions, shape data with interfaces and unions, then build the TypeScript you use in real apps: type guards for unknown API data, generics, utility and mapped types, and a typed CRUD client. Later modules cover classes and access modifiers, enums vs literal unions, declaration merging, and strict null handling.
outcomes: Read and write parameter and return type annotations
Recognize where TypeScript infers types for you
Narrow union values before using type-specific behavior
Use generics, keyof, readonly arrays, and partial updates for safer APIs
Validate unknown data with type guards and assertion functions, and make switches exhaustive with never
Write constrained generics and typed helpers with keyof and indexed access types
Derive types with Pick, Omit, Record, Required, Readonly, mapped types, template literal types, as const, and satisfies
Type a CRUD client end to end: DTOs, discriminated API results, and field-keyed form errors
Use access modifiers, readonly, and parameter properties in classes, and know they are compile-time only
Choose between enums and literal unions derived from as const
Explain interface declaration merging and augment global and library types
Handle possibly-undefined values under strictNullChecks and noUncheckedIndexedAccess
